messages:
aisha: Heads-up — saw 3 OOMs on gpu-4 during the midnight canary. stack points to kv_cache alloc path, not GPU OOMs. anyone seen this pattern before?
miguel: Can you paste the minimal logs/stack you have?
aisha: sure, snippet below:
```
[2026-03-10T00:12:33Z] ERROR runtime: kv_cache_alloc failed: requested 1.2G, available 512M
stack: runtime/kv/cache.go:223 allocKV -> pageAlloc -> kernel_select
```
dave: Are these long-context sessions (long token histories) or a sudden spike in concurrency?
aisha: mostly long-chat sessions — turns >6k tokens. reuse miss rate rises, fragmentation increases over time.
sophia: perf profiling earlier showed slab fragmentation creeping up across long-lived sessions. bucket occupancy drifted from 52% -> 78% over 12h and effective free dropped under 200MB before the OOM.
miguel: ok. immediate mitigations we can consider: 1) short-term: aggressive prefix eviction for long sessions 2) reduce batch window to limit concurrent alloc spikes 3) soft-degrade: switch to compact KV kernel that trades perf for memory 4) fallback to smaller model variant for affected routes
oncall-tom: I like 1+2 as immediate hotfixes. also think we need a short-circuit to prevent hard OOM: when free_kv < threshold emit kv_soft_degrade and free up oldest ~20% slots, switch kernel and mark request with header X-KV-Degraded.
dave: What about client-visible behavior — should we 429/retry or degrade silently to a smaller model? 429 might break user flows.
aisha: 429 is disruptive for most customers. degrade is preferable if we can guarantee no silent correctness regressions for opted-in tenants. should be opt-in per-tenant.
miguel: rollout plan: (A) implement kv_soft_degrade flag + metrics (kv_degrade_count, kv_eviction_count), (B) deploy to canary pool, monitor kv_eviction_rate, latency p95, and quality regressions on eval set, (C) expand if stable.
sophia: I'll add perf counters: slab_waste_bytes, contiguous_run_count, local_reuse_hit_rate. also propose kernel-selection tweak: prefer dense (compact) kernel when fragmentation metric > 0.65 to avoid new allocations.
ops-bot: Deploy queued: release/kv-soft-degrade v0.1 -> canary cluster at 03:30 UTC :rocket:
dave: add a quick-runbook snippet in devex about the toggle (--kv-degrade-threshold) and steps to revert if latency regresses. include an alert that fires when kv_degrade_count > 5/min.
aisha: I'll draft an incident note + attach reproducer (long-session script) after the deploy. thanks team :thumbsup:
miguel: one more — ensure we capture sample stack traces and a memory slab snapshot on OOM and upload to S3 for triage. otherwise it's hard to correlate fragmentation windows.
oncall-tom: agreed. I'll own the rollback/playbook if canary shows >2% p95 latency regression.
sophia: For longer term, we should consider slab compaction background worker and a compact-on-evict path; but that's bigger. short-term soft-degrade should buy time.
aisha: OK closing for now. will update thread after canary results.
